raw.title: refactor: derive describe method/target from the canonical classifier
raw.body:
refactor: derive describe method/target from the canonical classifier

The CLI and MCP describe surfaces each carried a private copy of the
operationPath parser, diverging from arazzo-spec's canonical classifier
in two user-visible ways: they uppercased lowercase verbs ("get /pets"
displayed a method and URL the runtime never resolves), and they
invented a body-based default method for unsupported specification-form
values the runtime refuses before deriving any method.

Both copies are deleted. arazzo-spec gains presented_method_and_target,
which derives the pair the way the engine does: case-sensitive method
token via split_operation_method, the engine's POST/GET body default,
and no invented method for unsupported forms (method: null; the schemas
already declare method nullable). Step list rendering shows method-less
targets instead of hiding them behind "---".

Pinned by a presentation table test beside the classifier, output.rs's
first unit tests, and an MCP build_step_summary test. Drift guards and
schemas unchanged. Closes finding F5 in the 2026-08-22 rust-code-smell
audit, recorded in the audit doc.
